provenance: Colour NAMES come from museum documentation (Louvre press material, room notes, conservation reports) or from the building itself. HEX VALUES are approximations authored for this project by eye from photographs and named-colour references; they are NOT spectrophotometer samples. Every consumer should treat hex as the art direction value, not as measured paint.

red-madder.name: Rouge de garance / madder red
red-madder.where: Salles Rouges, Denon level 1, rooms 700-702 (Grande Odalisque, Coronation, Raft of the Medusa, Liberty)
red-madder.note: Deep, slightly brownish red. The single most recognisable wall colour in the museum.

red-madder-deep.name: Madder red, shaded vignette
red-madder-deep.where: Lower wall band and reveals of the same rooms
red-madder-deep.note: Use for the picture rail band and door reveals so the flat wall does not read as plastic.

midnight-blue.name: Bleu de Prusse / midnight blue
midnight-blue.where: Salle des Etats, room 711 (Mona Lisa, Wedding at Cana), repaint of 2019
midnight-blue.note: Louvre calls it 'a very dense shade of blue enriched with subtle variations of black'. Nothing else in the palace is this colour.

ochre.name: Ochre / ocre jaune
ochre.where: Denon Egyptian rooms and the Denon stair halls; pre-2019 Salle des Etats

ochre-earth.name: Terre d'ocre profonde
ochre-earth.where: Sully level 0 rooms on the Egyptian side

stone-grey.name: Pierre de Paris, pale
stone-grey.where: Sully Greek galleries 345-348 (Venus de Milo rooms)
stone-grey.note: Neutral warm grey. Keeps marble statuary readable.

slate-green.name: Vert d'ardoise
slate-green.where: Richelieu level 0 Mesopotamian and sculpture rooms

ochre-light.name: Ocre clair
ochre-light.note: Lighter and cleaner than the Denon ochre.

crimson-silk.name: Rouge impérial / crimson silk damask
crimson-silk.where: Napoleon III Apartments, room 544 Grand Salon
crimson-silk.note: A textile colour, not a paint. Render with a damask weave normal, not flat.

apollon-blue.name: Bleu de la Galerie d'Apollon
apollon-blue.where: Galerie d'Apollon, room 705, ground behind the gilded stucco
apollon-blue.note: Deep lapis-like blue, always adjacent to gold leaf.

egypt-dark.name: Grise-brune des salles egyptiennes
egypt-dark.note: Dark, low-reflectance, so the pink granite sphinx separates.

white-plaster.name: Platre blanc
white-plaster.note: Never pure white; the Louvre whites are warm.

stone-cream.name: Pierre de Chassagne, clair
stone-cream.where: Hall Napoleon walls, undercroft; the concrete ceiling is tinted with the same stone dust
stone-cream.note: Cool pale beige, drawn from the Chassagne stone cladding.

stone-limestone-warm.name: Calcaire luteien, appareille
stone-limestone-warm.where: Exterior and courtyard walls read as flat colour in the distance
stone-limestone-warm.note: Same value as stone.limestone-warm for walls seen at frame-fill distance.

parquet-versailles.name: Parquet de Versailles
parquet-versailles.geometry: Square panels 0.90 m, each inlaid with a diagonal chevron; oak, matte oil finish.
parquet-versailles.where: Denon level 1 painting rooms, Grande Galerie

parquet-poitiers.name: Parquet a la Poitiers
parquet-poitiers.geometry: Herringbone, planks 0.55 m long at 45 degrees, no panel borders.

marble-checker.name: Dallage de marbre en damier
marble-checker.geometry: Alternating pale and warm-grey marble slabs, 0.60 m, thin dark joint; occasional larger 1.20 m border course.
marble-checker.where: Galerie d'Apollon, Richelieu grand stair, Napoleon III apartments

stone-flag.name: Dalles de pierre
stone-flag.geometry: Cut limestone flags 1.2 x 0.8 m, 8 mm joints, honed.
stone-flag.where: Sully level 0 Greek and Egyptian galleries

pave-granite.name: Paves de gres et granit
pave-granite.geometry: Cour Napoléon: small sandstone and granite setts in fan pattern, 650,000 of them (Louvre figure). Cour Carree: a granite cross of Plaintel slabs with four compartments of small Fontainebleau sandstone setts between the arms.
pave-granite.where: Cour Napoleon, Place du Carrousel, Cour Carree

hall-napoleon-stone.name: Pierre beige de Chassagne
hall-napoleon-stone.geometry: Large honed limestone panels on the walls of the Hall Napoleon, with a white concrete ceiling tinted from the same stone dust.

cream-cove.name: Corniche creme
cream-cove.where: Denon salles, cove and picture rail

gold-leaf.name: Dorure a la feuille
gold-leaf.where: Galerie d'Apollon vault, Napoleon III salons, picture frames

glazed-skylight.name: Verriere
glazed-skylight.where: Grande Galerie, Salle des Etats, Cour Marly, Cour Puget, Cour Khorsabad

marble-rouge.name: Marbre rouge antique
marble-rouge.where: Pilasters flanking the Venus de Milo room (Louvre trail: 'between the red marble pillars')

wood-oak.name: Chene
wood-oak.where: Dutch rooms: door cases and skirting

pyramid-tint.name: Verre feuillete 21 mm, Saint-Gobain
pyramid-tint.note: Near-colourless; the pyramid reads green only from accumulated thickness.

gilt-frame.name: Cadre dore
gilt-frame.note: Every heroic painting in the route hangs in a gilded frame about 12 cm wide with a 3 cm sight edge.

pentelic.name: Marbre du Pentelique
pentelic.note: Borghese Gladiator; slightly warmer and more translucent than Carrare.
